label: late original-phase steps (t>=5) in sequences starting with n/0/e/c
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.01% of steps). 96% of its mass is in the original phase at positions 5-8 (just before <DEL>; to_go 0-2), mostly in long sequences (L=8-9). Within those steps it is strongly gated by the first original token: n, 0, e, c (lift 5-8x), with w weaker. Nearly silent at t<4, on the delimiter, and in the copy phase. The predicate covers ~86% of activations and mass, but precision is under 1%: only a small, hash-like subset of matching steps fire. Adding further conditions (third token m/v/o, second token 0/e/w/o/v, current input p/t/r/h/1/i) raises precision to ~9% but halves recall, so the feature looks like a sparse conjunction over the remembered prefix plus the current input, not a clean single concept. Magnitude is roughly flat (median 0.12, max 0.26); the strongest examples have prefix n/e/0/c followed by w/v/o and m/v at position 2.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+4.38), orig0=0 (+4.06), orig0=e (+3.97), orig0=c (+3.71), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+3.59), orig2=m (+3.13). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-4.18), prev3_tok=- (-3.20), t=4 (-1.77), next_out=- (-1.49).
